description: GENERATORS — music you do not have to write. BAND generators (has: ["band"] — jazz …; more genres are added without a release) write a WHOLE arranged piece in a genre: every part's notes (drums, bass, piano, a lead), its form and changes, for a seed. With generator + bars | seconds, bpm, key, seed, lead ("none" = rhythm section alone) → parts[] ({name, instrument, timbre_preset, notes}), form, changes and the .mid (midi_base64): free, instant, no audio. To HEAR it: doseedo_render_score {generator: {id, seed, bars, key, lead}, bpm} plays that exact piece — you pass no notes — and doseedo_mix {from_job} mixes it in the genre's own style (mix_style: a dub's spring tank and tape echo). A film cue or a song that calls for a generator's genre should use it rather than be composed. DRUM generators — ready-made kits and grooves: each generator is a KIT (recorded one-shots for a genre: doseedo_render_midi plays your drum notes through it when the part's drum_genre names it), a LOOP (a groove written for a seed: doseedo_generate_loop → the audio + its MIDI), or both (house, deep house, tech house, afro house, jackin' house — the list grows without a release, so read it rather than remember it). No args → every generator: id, what it has, the drum_genre words that reach its kit, its loop's tempo, swing and bars. With generator (+ bars, bpm, seed, swing, fills, percussion) → that generator's loop AS MIDI: notes[] [{pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity}] (GM drums) and the .mid (midi_base64) — the SAME groove doseedo_generate_loop plays for that seed, instant, free, no audio: read a few seeds, pick or edit one, then render it (doseedo_generate_loop with the same seed, or doseedo_render_midi with your edited notes) or put it on a session track (set_midi_notes). Read-only, no key needed.

bpm.description: Tempo written into the .mid, 40–240 (default: the generator's).

direction.description: A BAND generator: what you want of the piece, as doseedo_render_score's generator takes it — {dynamics: [{at_seconds, level: none|low|medium|high|peak, ramp?}], hits: [{at_seconds, kind?: light|medium|full, who?, stroke?}] (who = only those parts land it; stroke = the one drum of the kit that sounds: kick, snare, rim, clap, hat, open hat, crash, tom, high tom, floor tom), lay_out: [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who?, only?}] (who rests: no name = the lead; a part, a family, "rhythm", "all"; no times with who or only = the whole piece), thin: [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, to?: beats|halves|bars, who?}] (who plays thinner: keeps only the beats / the bar's halves / the bar lines), texture: [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who, plays?: held|pedal|pulse|arpeggio|ostinato|walk|stabs|comp|line|four_on_the_floor|backbeat|half_time|light|full, value?, level?}] (what a part plays there — taken from the style's own writing for that part over the same chords, never invented; not applied where the style does not play it), textures: true (the answer lists what each part can play: textures), articulation: [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who, style}] (HOW the named parts are played there: legato | staccato | marcato | accent | spiccato | tenuto | portato | espressivo | senza_vibrato … — a passage on their articulation, no note changed; pizzicato, tremolo, harmonics and mutes are another sound, not a style), builds: [{into_seconds, beats?, drop?}], ending: {kind: cut|button|ring|fade, at_seconds?, strength?, build?} (build: true = the band builds into the last chord), intro: false, swing: light|medium|hard, solo_swing: straight|light|medium|hard} — YOUR OWN BAND: band: [{instrument, timbre_preset?, name?, chair?}] (who is seated in place of the generator's own players) — and YOUR OWN MUSIC for it to arrange: theme: {notes: [[pitch, beat, beats, velocity], …] (beats from the tune's first bar line), statements?: [{at_seconds, on?, from_beat?, beats?, octave?, transpose?, stretch?, mode?: major|minor (the statement in the parallel mode of the theme's tonic), harmony?: [{on, at: third_below|third_above|sixth_below|sixth_above|octave_below|octave_above}] (parts that play it WITH its carrier at that interval)}]} (the generator's own tune comes out and yours goes in, every note as written — with no statements, wherever its own tune was), changes: "Dm | Bb | Gm | A" (your chords, one cell a bar, as a loop; left out with a theme, the chords are harmonised to the theme). STYLE TRANSFER — song: {melody: [[pitch, beat, beats], …], changes: "C | Am | F | G7" (one cell a bar, the WHOLE song), sections: [{label, bars}], meter?, bpm?, key?, phrasing?} plays YOUR SONG in this genre and keeps it exactly: its length, its sections, its chart bar for bar and every note of its tune from bar one (every pitch, in order, sung in the genre's phrasing: an eighth early where the genre pushes the beat or its band pushes the change, its eighths swung in a swing; phrasing: "as written" keeps every onset exactly); the generator decides only how its chairs play it (lead: "none" = the genre's band without the tune). A melody alone is harmonised; chords alone get the genre's own tune; parts: [{name, notes}] (a MIDI arrangement) is read for its tune and chart. A genre in another metre (a waltz, 6/8, 12/8) plays the song re-metered by the meter-change rule and says what moved. only: "bass" | ["bass", "drums"] returns just those parts — the genre's line for one stem, written with the whole band. Times in seconds at this bpm, or at_beats / from_beats / to_beats / into_beats.

fills.description: false = no fills at the phrase ends.

generator.description: A generator id ("deep_house") or genre words ("afro house") → its loop as MIDI. Omit to list the generators.

key.description: A BAND generator: the key, e.g. "F", "C minor" (default: drawn by the seed).

lead.description: A BAND generator: the lead instrument (one of its leads), or "none" for the rhythm section alone.

percussion.description: Percussion voices, 0–4 (default: drawn by the seed).

seconds.description: A BAND generator: the piece's length in seconds (4–600) instead of bars — a film cue's duration.

seed.description: Which groove: the same seed is the same pattern (default 1).

name: doseedo_generators
title: Generators (a band's whole piece in a genre; drum kits, grooves, loop MIDI)
